newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks end down but well off lows.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks end down but well off lows.

text.p: Australian shares ended slightly weaker but off their lows on Monday with the resource sector pinned down by a strong Australian dollar.

The key share barometer, the All Ordinaries Index, closed 3.5 points lower at 2,385.1, well off its intra-day low of 2,372.6. The December share price index ended up six points at 2,392.0 and at a 6.9 point premium to the underlying index.

Stocks ended narrowly mixed, with major resource issues finishing mostly weaker and the industrial sector also ending down but aided by stronger building materials and developer and contractor sectors.

"Early focus was on the stronger dollar but good building approvals data helped the building materials companies and generally lent the market some better sentiment this afternoon," a Sydney-based dealer said.
The dealer said as building approvals data was usually lumpy the market's response suggested investors were looking for excuses to buy the market rather than focusing on negative factors.
"The market finished on the way up. Another good night on Wall Street may give it enough juice to push it through 2400 again tommorrow," he said.

One of the busiest stocks was transport group TNT whose shares ended firmer at A$2.45 following the news on Friday that Dutch postals and telecoms group PTT Nederland NV (KPN) had gained control of the company.
KPN's A$2 billion bid is now free from conditions and analysts expect the company to receive acceptances rapidly now that major stakeholder Bankers Trust has relinquished its 19.9 percent stake.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trade saw moderate activity while options trade was slow. Total options traded 24,629 (29,429).
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 8.162 (5,639).
In other markets, local bond yields ended near to the year's recent lows as the market found renewed confidence after last week's heavy selling, triggered by Friday's solid U.S. trend.
The yield on 10-year T-bonds closed at 7.08 percent, down 0.12 percentage points from Friday's close.
The Australian dollar stormed to fresh six year highs as a break of key resistance in New York sparked heavy catch-up buying from Asian investors.
At 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), the dollar was quoted at US$0.8199/04.
